key_insight: The paper shows that isothermal no-slip walls in compressible Navier-Stokes can be made entropy-stable by adding a temperature-weighted affine term to entropy, enabling exact wall balance without suppressing heat transfer.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical path to robust high-order CFD boundary treatments for heated walls, improving stability and conservation in turbulence and compressible flow simulations.
method: Defines an affine entropy / ballistic-energy modification for stationary isothermal walls.
Derives two entropy-stable DG-SBP-SAT wall formulations: complete-residual and Fourier-energy-exact.
Uses pointwise identities, manufactured solutions, and 3D test cases to verify balance and convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pointwise identity checks, manufactured-solution convergence at about p_s+1 in discrete L2, thermal-relaxation balance tests, and 3D closed-domain and curved-wall demonstrations.
watch_item: The formulation assumes a stationary, impermeable, no-slip wall at constant positive temperature, so extensions to moving walls or more general thermal boundary conditions may need additional work.
paper_title: Isothermal walls in the compressible Navier-Stokes equations: affine entropy, ballistic energy, and entropy-stable discrete formulations
